title: Brijuni with Teenagers: Family Travel Guide 2027
metaDescription: Brijuni with teens in 2027: ticket prices, bike routes, snorkeling at Verige, safari park, boat from Fažana, hotels and tips for a day or overnight stay.
content:
## How Do You Get to Brijuni from Fažana?

The only way onto Veliki Brijun, the main island, is the park's own boat from Fažana. The crossing covers about 2 km and takes 15 minutes. Fažana is roughly 8 km north of Pula, so Pula is the usual base for families. In April, May and October there are about 3–5 departures a day. In summer there are more.

Tickets carry a fixed departure time. The park does not allow earlier or later boarding, and the ticket is not refunded or moved to another date. Teenagers who oversleep cost the family money, so book the first or second boat and build in a buffer.

## Brijuni Ticket Prices for Teens and Parents

The guided excursion costs €50 per adult from June to September and €35 from October to May. Children aged 7–18 pay €20 in summer and €15 off-season. Students and over-65s pay €40 or €30. Under-7s go free. The ticket covers the return boat, insurance, a guide, the tourist train, the safari park and the museum displays.

The self-guided ticket uses the Brijuni Pocket Guide app and costs €40 in summer and €30 off-season. A €15 evening ticket is sold in July and August from 6 pm.

The €50 peak fare applies until 30 September and drops to €35 on 1 October. Moving a visit by a few days saves €15 per adult.

## Best Activities for Teenagers on Brijuni

### Cycling the 13.3 km loop
Cycling is the best activity on the island. The route is paved, easy and takes about 1 hour 10 minutes of riding time. Cars are almost absent, so teens can ride freely. Bike rental cost about €5 per person per hour in May 2026, and peak-season prices may be higher. The loop passes the golf course, the safari park, Roman ruins, forest and the coast. Electric cars and scooters are also available for rent.

The train-only excursion is the weaker choice for teens. Sitting through a one-hour commentary on a train sounds fine on paper, but most 14–17-year-olds lose interest by the second stop. Choose the self-guided ticket and bikes instead.

### Snorkeling at Verige Bay
Verige Bay holds the remains of a 1st-century Roman villa rustica and the Temple of Venus. An underwater educational trail of roughly 500 m runs along the shore, and the submerged ruins are visible from the surface in clear water. Bring your own mask and snorkel. Saluga Bay, further along the loop, has a beach for swimming.

### Safari Park and Ethno Park
The safari park covers about 9 ha and has zebras, llamas, ostriches and Lanka, an Indian elephant. Allow about an hour. The Ethno Park next to it has Istrian boškarin oxen, pramenka sheep, donkeys and goats.

### Dinosaur footprints and the old olive tree
The dinosaur footprints are along the coast and are a fast stop on the bike route. The olive tree is about 1,600 years old. Both take 10–15 minutes each.

### Walking and kayaking
The Zelenikovac circular educational trail starts on the north coast and runs through forest and fields to Verige Bay. Coastal kayaking and snorkeling in the protected marine area are also offered by the park.

## Boat Trips from Fažana: Dolphins and Swimming

Private operators in Fažana run panorama and sunset dolphin trips around the park from about €18–30 per person. Trips last 1.5 to 2.5 hours. Many include a swim stop. Boats do not dock at Veliki Brijun on these trips, so they are not a substitute for a visit to the island.

Some trips stop at Sveti Jerolim island, where entry is €7 for adults and about €3–4 for children, paid in cash. Dolphin sightings are never guaranteed. Treat the dolphins as a bonus, not the reason to book.

## Day Trip or Overnight Stay?

A day trip works for most families. Self-guided visitors typically spend 5–8 hours. A stay on the island suits families who want quiet evenings after the day-trippers leave. Accommodation is limited. Hotel Neptun and Hotel Karmen are on Veliki Brijun, and there are villas. Prices are high and rooms should be booked months ahead. Staying in Pula and visiting for a day is the cheaper option.

## Local Tips for Families with Teens

- Book the first boat of the day, then rent bikes on arrival. Bike stock is limited when a full boat lands at once.
- Bring water, sunscreen and swimwear. Shops on the island are few and prices are higher than in Fažana.
- Carry cash. Some extras, such as Sveti Jerolim entry, are cash only.
- The best months are May, June and September. The sea is warm and crowds are thinner than in July and August.
- In July and August, the €15 evening ticket gives a cooler visit and a return boat as late as 23:00.
- The island has few shaded stretches in midday heat. Plan the ride for the morning.

## Is Brijuni Worth It for Teenagers?

Yes, if the day includes cycling and swimming. The island has no nightlife, arcades or shopping, so teens who need constant stimulation will be bored by the afternoon. Pair Brijuni with an evening in Pula, where the Roman amphitheatre and waterfront cafés give teens more to do.

faq.question: Is Brijuni good for teenagers?
faq.answer: Yes, for active teens. Cycling, snorkeling at Verige Bay, the safari park and swimming fill a full day. There is no nightlife, so plan evening activities in Pula.

faq.question: How much does Brijuni cost for a family with teens?
faq.answer: In summer, the guided excursion costs €50 per adult and €20 per child aged 7–18. A family of two adults and two teens pays about €140, before bike rental at around €5 per person per hour. Off-season fares are €35 and €15.

faq.question: How long does it take to visit Brijuni?
faq.answer: The guided excursion takes about four hours, including the 15-minute crossing each way. Self-guided visitors with bikes usually stay 5–8 hours. The 13.3 km cycling loop takes about 1 hour 10 minutes of riding, plus stops.

faq.question: Can you rent bikes on Brijuni?
faq.answer: Yes, bikes are rented on Veliki Brijun. The rate was about €5 per person per hour in May 2026. Electric cars and scooters are also available.

faq.question: Can you snorkel on Brijuni?
faq.answer: Yes. Verige Bay has an underwater educational trail of roughly 500 m past a submerged Roman villa. Bring your own snorkel gear, or choose a boat tour that supplies it.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Brijuni with teens?
faq.answer: May, June and September combine warm sea with thinner crowds. October is cheaper, with the €35 adult fare, but the sea is cooler.

quickAnswer: Brijuni suits teenagers best as a bike-and-swim day trip. Take the 15-minute park boat from Fažana, rent bikes for the 13.3 km loop, snorkel the Roman ruins in Verige Bay and see the safari park. Teen tickets (ages 7–18) cost about €20 in summer; adults pay about €50.
